content:
## Palo Alto Networks, Inc. (PANW) `[Software & SaaS]`
- Morgan Stanley raised its price target to **$410** and maintained an **Overweight** rating; Wedbush initiated coverage at **Outperform** with a **$400** target. (Morgan Stanley note; Wedbush note)
- Palo Alto Networks’ Unit 42 launched **Continuous Frontier AI Defense**, a subscription service using Anthropic and OpenAI models with Palo Alto threat intelligence. (Unit 42/company announcement)
- Bernstein rated PANW **Market Perform** with a **$351** target, while Daiwa raised its target to **$390** and maintained **Buy**. (Bernstein note; Daiwa note)

## CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. (CRWD) `[Software & SaaS]`
- No company-specific catalyst found in window.
- CRWD, PANW, and OKTA rose together while the **QQQ ETF fell 0.7%**, indicating a cybersecurity-sector rotation; PANW was the lead stock named in the Wednesday market-mover coverage. (Yahoo Finance)

## Palantir Technologies Inc. (PLTR) `[AI Infrastructure]`
- Rosenblatt reaffirmed a **Buy** rating and assigned a **$225** price target. (Rosenblatt note)
- Surf Air Mobility appointed **Barrett Brown** to lead **SurfOS**, its AI-enabled operating system powered by Palantir software. (Surf Air Mobility announcement)
- Palantir’s AI sovereignty strategy was highlighted in coverage of its recent AIPCon, with sovereign control of data, infrastructure, and AI systems identified as a central commercial theme. (Palantir AIPCon coverage)

## BP p.l.c. (BP) `[Specialty Materials & IP Licensing]`
- J.P. Morgan upgraded BP from **Neutral to Overweight** and raised its price target from **550 pence to 675 pence**, equivalent to approximately **$54** for the ADR. (J.P. Morgan note)
- J.P. Morgan projected that BP’s total financial obligations could fall **50% by the end of 2027** and estimated upstream volume growth of approximately **3% annually from 2030 to 2035**. (J.P. Morgan note)

## ServiceNow, Inc. (NOW) `[Software & SaaS]`
- No company-specific catalyst found in window.

## Equinor ASA (EQNR) `[Specialty Materials & IP Licensing]`
- No company-specific catalyst found in window.

## Fortinet, Inc. (FTNT) `[Software & SaaS]`
- No company-specific catalyst found in window.
- Fortinet was identified by Josh Brown as one of three preferred cybersecurity stocks alongside **CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Networks**, with cybersecurity-sector strength cited as the relevant group catalyst. (Josh Brown/Ritholtz commentary)

## ConocoPhillips (COP) `[Specialty Materials & IP Licensing]`
- No company-specific catalyst found in window.

## TotalEnergies SE (TTE) `[Specialty Materials & IP Licensing]`
- J.P. Morgan downgraded TotalEnergies from **Overweight to Neutral**. (J.P. Morgan note)
- J.P. Morgan cited TotalEnergies’ **highest direct Middle East asset exposure among European companies** and the possibility of windfall taxes. (J.P. Morgan note)

## T-Mobile US, Inc. (TMUS) `[Wireless & Mobile]`
- No company-specific catalyst found in window.

## Okta, Inc. (OKTA) `[Software & SaaS]`
- Scotiabank raised its price target from **$165 to $190** and maintained a **Sector Outperform** rating. (Scotiabank note)
- BTIG raised its price target from **$187 to $219** and reiterated **Buy**, citing customer and partner feedback on Okta’s AI Agents products. (BTIG note)
- Baird raised its target to **$200** and maintained **Outperform**; Bank of America raised its target from **$170 to $200** while maintaining **Neutral**. (Baird note; Bank of America note)
- Wells Fargo raised its target to **$200** and cited AI-driven demand; the **Oktane ’26** conference was identified as a forthcoming company event. (Wells Fargo note)
